name: Generative and Style-based Models
text:
# Generative and Style-based Models

Also called: 3D-aware generative models, NeRF-GAN hybrids

## Overview
This family integrates generative adversarial networks (GANs) or diffusion models with [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) to synthesize novel 3D-consistent images from noise or text, rather than optimizing a single static scene from photographs. Unlike [standard NeRF training](#985-nerf-training-loop-with-random-ray-batching.md) which fits a specific dataset, these models learn a distribution of 3D shapes and textures. They are distinguished from siblings like [AdaNeRF](6195-adanerf.md) (which adapts a pre-trained [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) to new views) by generating the radiance field parameters or latent codes directly from a generative prior, enabling the creation of novel objects [S1].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family compute a radiance field function $f_\theta(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ that outputs volume density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ (or latent features) for a query point $\mathbf{x}$ and direction $\mathbf{d}$. The final pixel color $\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{r})$ for a ray $\mathbf{r}$ is computed via the [standard volume rendering](#1165-standard-volume-rendering-equation.md) integral:
$$
\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{c}_i
$$
where $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$ and $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$. The architectural variations lie in how $\sigma_i$ and $\mathbf{c}_i$ are generated from the input coordinates, how the network is structured (depth, width, connectivity), and what auxiliary inputs (embeddings, priors, features) are fused into the computation.

## Subtopics

### [HyperNeRFGAN](8765-hypernerfgan.md)
Generates 3D representations by using a hypernetwork (StyleGAN2) to produce the weights of a simplified NeRF target network. It solves the problem of 3D-aware image generation when camera positions are unavailable by removing viewing directions from the NeRF input. Unlike [Latent-NeRF](9110-latent-nerf.md) which optimizes latent codes for specific instances, [HyperNeRFGAN](#8765-hypernerfgan.md) generates network parameters themselves, allowing synthesis from noise.

### [Latent-NeRF](9110-latent-nerf.md)
Optimizes NeRFs by integrating pre-trained latent diffusion models, enabling high-quality novel view synthesis and text-guided editing without dense 3D supervision. It distinguishes itself by operating in a compact latent space (4 channels) rather than RGB color space, using score distillation from Stable Diffusion to guide optimization.

### StyleNeRF
A 3D-aware generative model that merges 3D scene representation with style-based generative models [S1]. It uses NeRF to generate low-resolution feature maps and samples them to high resolution to avoid the super-computation cost of full volume rendering [S1]. It applies regularization terms to improve 3D consistency, addressing issues with view-dependent conditions and noise injection [S1].

## Background
The intersection of NeRF and GANs began with [GRAF](#8539-graf.md) (Schwarz et al., 2020), which introduced a discriminator to control shape and appearance for single-object scenes [S1]. This was extended by GIRAFFE (Niemeyer et al., 2021) to handle multi-object scenes by decomposing shape, appearance, and background, and by pi-GAN (Chan et al., 2021) which used periodic activation functions for high-quality 3D-aware synthesis [S1]. However, these methods required large datasets and were limited to simple geometries like faces or cars [S1]. Subsequent works like HyperNeRFGAN and [Latent-NeRF](#9110-latent-nerf.md) addressed these limitations by leveraging hypernetworks and diffusion models respectively to improve scalability and text controllability [S1].
